chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from 'Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any Muslim who is between two other Muslims apostatizes from Islam, denies the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and rejects him, then his blood is permissible for whoever hears that from him, and his wife is separated from him on the day he apostatizes, and his wealth is divided among his heirs, and his wife observes the waiting period of the one whose husband has died, and it is upon the Imam to kill him if they bring him to him, and he does not ask him if he wants to return (to Islam).'

key_terms.عِدَّةَ الْمُتَوَفَّى: The waiting period of the deceased
key_terms.يَسْتَتِيبَهُ: Asks him if he wants to return (to Islam)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific legal consequences for a Muslim who apostatizes in the presence of others according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific legal consequences of apostasy (*riddah*), emphasizing the immediate separation of the wife and the Imam's authority to execute the apostate without the customary period of repentance (*istitab*). It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the apostate's blood becomes *mubah* (permissible) for anyone who hears the declaration, distinguishing it from other schools that may require a waiting period for repentance.
